After releasing the public betas of macOS 27, iPadOS 27, iOS 27, and other updates announced at WWDC26 yesterday, Apple is now rolling out the first public betas for AirPods Max 2, AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2, and AirPods (4th generation). Details below.

The first public AirPods firmware betas are now available

At last month's WWDC26, Apple announced several new AirPods features that will arrive alongside iOS 27 and other upcoming operating system updates.

These include custom EQ controls that let users personalize the sound of their AirPods, as well as expanded GymKit support that allows AirPods Pro 3 users to sync heart rate data via iPhone.

Apple is also bringing firmware betas to AirPods Max 2 for the first time, available for enrollment through devices running iOS 27 or macOS 27.

After launching the first public betas of iOS 27 and Apple's other upcoming operating systems yesterday, Apple has now released the first public beta firmware updates for the following AirPods models:

  • AirPods Max 2
  • AirPods Pro 3
  • AirPods Pro 2
  • AirPods Pro 2 (USB-C)
  • AirPods (4th generation)
  • AirPods (4th generation, Active Noise Cancellation)

The build number for AirPods firmware version 9.0.314 is 9A5314b, the same as last week's developer beta.

Installing the AirPods firmware beta

Below is the official guide from Apple on how to register eligible AirPods for the firmware beta program:

Enable beta updates On a Mac running the macOS 27 beta or later: To enable AirPods beta, connect your AirPods to your Mac via Bluetooth settings. Go to System Settings > Bluetooth, then select (i) next to your AirPods. In the AirPods settings menu, scroll down to find "AirPods beta updates." Use the toggle to enable beta software updates. On an iPhone or iPad running the iOS 27 beta or later: To enable AirPods beta, connect your AirPods to your iOS device. Go to Settings > Bluetooth, then select (i) next to your AirPods. Apple notes that once users have enabled the "AirPods beta updates" option, the firmware update will install automatically "when your AirPods are in their charging case and near" a paired iPhone or Mac.
